deck_title: Torricelli-Bernoulli hydrostatic orifice jet vs naive constant-speed jet excess rig

cards.subtitle: Deterministic Evangelista Torricelli (1643, De Motu Gravium) & Daniel Bernoulli (1738, Hydrodynamica) hydrostatic orifice efflux law (v_jet = sqrt(2*g*h) where hydrostatic head h(u) = h_0/(1+u), conserving streamline mechanical energy 0.5*rho*v^2 = rho*g*h so the kinetic-to-potential energy ratio locks at E_k/E_p = 1.0000x across all 17 head-depletion stations u in [0.0000, 1.0000] with 0/17 violated stations) versus naive constant-speed particle emitters (v_naive = v_0 = const regardless of tank drainage, which violates Bernoulli energy conservation by h_0/h(u) = 1 + u up to 1.2500x at u=0.25, 1.5000x at u=0.50, and 2.0000x at half-head u=1.00 across 16/17 stations) and 64-layer vertical hydrostatic pressure integration.

cards.headline: Exact controls are useful; realism remains a separate job.
good_fit: Punctured water barrels, fuel-tank leaks, dam sluice gates, and fountain nozzles coupled to real-time reservoir water level h(t)
Quadratic tank drainage ODE dh/dt = -(A_orifice / A_tank) * C_d * sqrt(2*g*h) with exact parabolic level decay
Parabolic water-jet range X = 2 * sqrt(h * y_drop) contracting naturally as the tank empties
Closed-form velocity v = C_v * sqrt(2.0 * g * max(0.0, z_surface - z_orifice))
not_for: Constant-displacement positive-displacement hydraulic pumps driven by an external motor rather than gravity head
